headline: Software Surges, Breadth Holds Wide as Thursday Session Finds Its Footing
body_html:
Equities are posting broad gains at midday Thursday, with advancers outnumbering decliners by better than three-to-one across the 545-name universe — 422 stocks in the green versus 120 in the red. Software is the clear sector leader, up 1.8%, while Homebuilders add 1.48% and Industrials contribute 0.86%. The one sore spot: Semiconductors, off 1.01%, keeping a lid on the tech complex even as software names push higher.

The standout mover of the session is Snowflake, which has rocketed 23.17% intraday, making it the dominant story on the tape. Fellow software-adjacent name Datadog is also catching a bid, up 4.33%, reinforcing the theme that investors are rotating toward software on a relative basis. On the industrial side, Worthington Enterprises (+4.93%) and Alamo Group (+4.39%) are lending support to the broader cyclical recovery. Geopolitical tension in the Middle East is lifting crude to six-week highs, a tailwind for Energy even as that sector's gain of 0.31% remains modest.

Into the close, the key question is whether Semiconductors stabilize — storage names NetApp (-7.54%) and Western Digital (-3.10%) are dragging on hardware sentiment. Watch whether the software rally holds its lead or profit-taking narrows the gap before the bell.

briefs.headline: Snowflake Dominates the Tape With a Historic Intraday Run
briefs.body: Shares of Snowflake have surged 23.17% in Thursday's session, making the cloud-data platform the most dramatic single-name mover of the day by a wide margin. The move is lifting the broader Software-Data category and drawing attention from traders watching for follow-through into the close.

briefs.headline: Middle East Tensions Push Crude to Six-Week Peak
briefs.body: Oil prices reached their highest level in six weeks Thursday as escalating tensions in the Gulf region stoked supply-disruption concerns. Reuters reported that Iran has issued warnings regarding a potential Israeli strike on a Hezbollah-held ridge in south Lebanon, adding a new flashpoint to an already volatile geopolitical backdrop.

briefs.headline: Storage Hardware Stocks Bear the Brunt of Tech Selling
briefs.body: NetApp fell 7.54% and Western Digital shed 3.10% mid-session, making storage hardware the most punished corner of the technology landscape. The declines are pressuring the broader Semiconductors sector, which is down 1.01% — the only sector in the red across Thursday's tape.

briefs.headline: Victoria's Secret Leads Consumer Decliners After Sharp Drop
briefs.body: Shares of Victoria's Secret tumbled 11.19% intraday, making the apparel retailer the steepest decliner in the universe on Thursday. The move dragged on the Consumer sector even as the broader market advanced, underscoring selective pressure on discretionary names amid an otherwise constructive tape.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Quietly Post Second-Best Sector Gain
briefs.body: The Homebuilders group climbed 1.48% through midday, the second-strongest sector performance of the session behind Software. The move suggests rate-sensitive names are finding renewed appetite as bond markets recover, consistent with the broader risk-on tone characterizing Thursday's trade.

briefs.headline: Industrials Breadth Impresses as Multiple Names Crack Top Gainers
briefs.body: Worthington Enterprises, Alamo Group, and Core & Main each posted gains exceeding 4% Thursday, propelling Industrials to a 0.86% advance. The cluster of outperformers across building products, agricultural equipment, and distribution points to broad-based demand rather than a single catalyst driving the sector.
